newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds flat, yield spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds flat, yield spreads widen.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities traded virtually unchanged during a sluggish Thursday afternoon session, while yield spreads widened fractionally to Treasuries.
"Yield curves widened to Treasuries in the sense that the 10-year (Treasury note) didn't go down and (pass-throughs) did," said a West Coast trader.
One New York-based trader said he saw activity in higher coupon pass-throughs, noting that one dealer "bought the roll" of GNMA 9.0 percent coupons.
When traders buy the roll, they buy securities for a particular settlement date and sell them for later settlement, according to one trader.

Late on Thursday, pass-throughs were flat to 2/32 lower in coupons of 7.0 percent or smaller, and were flat to 2/32 lower in premium coupons. The 10-year Treasury note was up 1/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 1/32 at 99-11/32, yielding 108 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable FNMAs were down 2/32 at 99-10/32, and FHLMCs were off 3/32 at 99-14/32.
